Compactness leaves finitely many lattice fibers. Each is isometrically embedded and has Hausdorff dimension equal to its affine dimension, so q is their maximum and the q-dimensional mixed measure is the sum of the fiber measures. The maximal-dimensional fibers have finite positive measure and smaller fibers are null. A zero label has every source allocation zero, and positive total mass leaves at least one label.

Each positive fiber has a nonzero direction space. Choosing a vector outside the finite union of its proper orthogonal complements makes every nonzero integer multiple nonconstant on every such fiber. For any prescribed slopes satisfying the statement, pairwise tie sets are proper intrinsic affine hyperplanes and therefore null. Singleton label sets cause no ties.

The column weights in each source simplex are exactly nonnegative allocations summing to that fiber mass. Each gradient block of the integral of the maximum is the moment of the unique winner almost everywhere. The coordinate difference quotient bound and eventual stability of the winner off the tie sets justify dominated convergence for the partial derivatives and their continuity.

The support function adds over the weighted simplex summands. The uniform error bound follows from the supremum norm estimate for a finite maximum and compactness of the fibers. The ball in the direction space centered at a relative interior target gives coercivity in that direction space. A minimizer there has restricted gradient zero, and the residual of two points in the same affine hull is in the direction space. When the direction space vanishes the equality follows from membership in a singleton.

The minimal polytope face contains the target in its relative interior. An exposing vector maximizes separately on each summand, giving precisely the simplex of allowed labels for each source. Its perturbation changes all allowed scores by the same amount on that source. Every disallowed label has a strictly smaller coefficient and bounded baseline differences on a compact fiber. Finitely many such comparisons give one finite T with strict loss everywhere on the positive fibers. This also treats a vertex, the full face, and a fiber with only one allowed label.

A finite maximum covers all of C, including lower-dimensional or noninteger fibers. Each winner set is a compact convex intersection with at most k-1 proper halfspaces, and pairwise ties are mixed-null. Positive mass supplies a strict winner point, including the vacuous single-label case. The density of the ambient interior of C and openness of strict winning give ambient interior for every cell.

The cell mixed sets have positive q-dimensional Hausdorff measure and are subsets of S, so their Hausdorff dimensions are q. The measure on each is exactly the restriction of the original intrinsic measure. Its normalized barycenter lies in the compact convex cell and has base m_i/t_i, giving mixed membership when this base is integral. The finite union and pairwise null overlaps exhaust the mixed measure.
